conditions: At least two real observations; x-bar is their arithmetic mean. Unbiased estimation of population variance requires independent identically distributed observations with finite variance.

evidence: The formula defines the corrected sample variance for n>=2. For iid observations with mean mu and finite variance sigma^2, the identity sum (X_i-Xbar)^2=sum (X_i-mu)^2-n(Xbar-mu)^2 holds by expanding. Taking expectations yields n sigma^2-n(sigma^2/n)=(n-1)sigma^2. Dividing by n-1 makes the estimator unbiased; normality is not needed.
